wiki_text: In November 2025 the Mozambique LNG consortium decided to lift the force majeure declared in 2021, and on January 29, 2026 TotalEnergies announced the full restart of all project activities onshore and offshore. Construction resumed at the Afungi site with more than 4,000 workers mobilized and the project about 40% complete; the revised budget is approximately US$20.5 billion and first LNG is expected in 2029. The restart covers the two-train (Trains 1-2) project sanctioned in 2019; the Train 3-4 expansion has not been sanctioned.

topic: FID taken; hull launched; capacity and JV
wiki_text: Eni announced the final investment decision for the Coral North (Coral Norte) FLNG project on October 2, 2025. The 3.6 mtpa floating LNG unit will be moored in the Coral gas field in Area 4, with first LNG targeted in 2028. The project joint venture comprises Eni (50%, operator), CNPC (20%), Kogas (10%), ENH (10%) and ADNOC's subsidiary XRG (10%) — ExxonMobil is not a participant. The vessel's hull was launched at Samsung Heavy Industries' Geoje shipyard on January 16, 2026.

topic: Force majeure lifted; FID and start-year outlook
wiki_text: ExxonMobil lifted the force majeure on the Rovuma LNG project on November 20, 2025, as security conditions in Cabo Delgado eased. A final investment decision on the 18 mtpa project is anticipated in 2026, with first LNG exports expected by 2030.
